skill.description: Guides users through creating or updating AI skills with structured SKILL.md files, optional deep documentation, workflow templates, and validation checks. Designed for PAI-style skill directories while aligning with Anthropic skill conventions.
skill.summary: Create and update AI skills using structured templates, activation triggers, and validation checklists.

security_audit.summary: The static external-command findings are markdown fences, inline filenames, or local path references rather than executable Ruby backticks. The hardcoded URL is a placeholder example, not an active network call. One low-severity semantic concern remains because the workflow asks users to update global AI context without an explicit confirmation requirement.

remediation.issue: Global context edits can affect future AI behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before updating `${PAI_DIR}/global/KAI.md`, and limit the edit to the available_skills entry.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger external-command scanner noise.
remediation.suggestion: Use text fences for directory layouts and label placeholder commands as examples that must be reviewed before use.

content.user_title: Create AI Skills with Guided Templates
content.value_statement: Building reusable AI skills requires clear structure and activation rules. This skill provides templates, workflows, and validation checks for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to choose simple, complex, or agent-based skill structures.
Provides SKILL.md frontmatter and section patterns for new skills.
Includes templates for simple, complex, agent-powered, and deep documentation skills.
Defines workflows for creating new skills and updating existing skills.
Lists validation checks for placeholders, triggers, paths, references, and testing.
limitations: Designed around PAI directory conventions and may need adaptation for other environments.
Does not create files automatically; users or agents must apply the steps.
Template commands are placeholders and must be reviewed before use.
Does not perform marketplace packaging or security validation by itself.

use_cases.title: Create a New Personal Skill
use_cases.description: Define activation triggers, choose a structure, and draft a clear SKILL.md for a focused capability.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Skill Documentation
use_cases.description: Use shared templates and validation checks to keep skill files consistent across a repository.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Skill Structure
use_cases.description: Review an existing skill, choose an update type, and add workflows or examples without changing its purpose.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a focused capability.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use create-skill to design a simple skill for my goal. Ask for missing triggers, tools, and examples before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Right Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: User needs help deciding simple, complex, or agent-based format.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use create-skill to compare the available skill structures for this capability. Recommend the smallest structure that fits the workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to improve a current skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use create-skill to review this skill and suggest focused updates. Preserve current triggers unless there is a clear reason to change them.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Agent-Based Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for multi-agent workflow planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use create-skill to plan an agent-based skill. Define agent roles, handoffs, validation points, and when parallel work is appropriate.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for reviewing database migrations.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for trigger phrases, required tools, and review scope. It then recommends a simple SKILL.md with workflow sections and examples.

output_examples.input: Improve our research skill so it supports multiple specialists.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies this as an agent-based update. It proposes agent roles, handoff rules, parallel execution limits, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Check whether my new skill template is complete.
output: Confirms frontmatter and activation triggers are present.
Flags remaining placeholders and missing examples.
Suggests tests for natural language activation.

best_practices: Start with the smallest skill structure that supports the workflow.
Write activation triggers that match real user requests.
Replace every placeholder and test the skill with natural language prompts.
anti_patterns: Keeping generic template examples in a finished skill.
Adding complex workflow files before the use case needs them.
Changing global context files without explicit user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create or update AI skills with clear triggers, structure, examples, and validation steps.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create agent-based skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a template for skills that coordinate specialized agents and parallel work.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The files provide documentation and placeholder command examples that users must review.

faq.question: Is it tied to one directory layout?
faq.answer: It is written for PAI-style directories, so other projects may need path changes.

faq.question: What should I check before publishing a skill made with it?
faq.answer: Check triggers, placeholders, references, examples, and any changes to global context files.
